Introduction and meaning
Commutation of sentence. BNS restatement of IPC 54–55. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 54–55. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 5 is the rule on “Commutation of sentence”. The section provides that the appropriate Government may, without the consent of the offender, commute any punishment under this Sanhita to any other punishment in accordance with section 474 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 5 exists so that “Commutation of sentence” has a closed legal test in Chapter II — Of Punishments. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Death, life, imprisonment, forfeiture, fine, and community service. How sentences combine, commute and enhance.

The provision in detail
5. The appropriate Government may, without the consent of the offender, commute any punishment under this Sanhita to any other punishment in accordance with section 474 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

Definitions and key terms
“appropriate Government” — ,–– (a) in cases where the sentence is a sentence of death or is for an offence against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the Union extends, the Central Government.

Essential ingredients
1. The appropriate Government may, without the consent of the offender, commute any punishment under this Sanhita to any other punishment in accordance with section 474 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

Explanations
Explanation.–For the purposes of this section the expression “appropriate Government” means,––

(a) in cases where the sentence is a sentence of death or is for an offence against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the Union extends, the Central Government; and

(b) in cases where the sentence (whether of death or not) is for an offence against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the State extends, the Government of the State within which the offender is sentenced

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 5 (Commutation of sentence) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 5 (Commutation of sentence), Chapter II — Of Punishments.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) The appropriate Government may, without the consent of the offender, commute any punishment under this Sanhita to any other punishment in accordance with section 474 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 5 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Death, life, imprisonment, forfeiture, fine, and community service. How sentences combine, commute and enhance.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

learningObjectives: Identify the role of the appropriate Government.
Distinguish commutation from other sentencing or remission concepts.
Connect BNS s.5 with BNSS s.474.
enhancement.definition: BNS s.5 enables the appropriate Government, without the offender's consent, to commute a punishment under the Sanhita to another punishment in accordance with BNSS s.474, subject to the statutory framework.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Commutation changes the nature of the punishment imposed. The authority, statutory conditions and applicable procedure must be identified from the BNS and the cross-referenced BNSS provision.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: BNS s.5 Commutation of sentence. Body and Explanation (a)-(b) checked against the official Gazette text and match word for word. The Definitions and key terms entry is incomplete and not verified. Commentary and cases not verified.
essentialIngredients: There must be a punishment under the BNS to which the commutation provision applies.
Identify the appropriate Government under the statutory definition.
The Government's power is exercised in accordance with BNSS s.474.
The question must concern commutation rather than a different form of sentence administration.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: A good answer should separate three questions: what punishment was imposed, who is the statutory decision-maker, and what the cross-referenced BNSS provision permits. The offender's consent is expressly addressed by s.5, so it should not be assumed that consent is a prerequisite. Do not treat commutation as synonymous with remission or pardon; those concepts have different statutory and constitutional contexts.
examples: A person serving a sentence asks whether the punishment can be changed to another recognised punishment: identify s.5 and then examine BNSS s.474.
A problem asks which Government is relevant: apply the definition of appropriate Government in s.5 to the nature of the sentence and the law under which the offence was committed.
A question uses the word 'remission' when the facts actually concern substitution of one punishment for another: first identify the correct legal concept before applying s.5.

rows.left: Changes the punishment to another punishment within the statutory framework.
rows.right: Concerns reduction/alteration of the period or operation of a sentence under the applicable law.

rows.left: Start with BNS s.5 and BNSS s.474.
rows.right: Identify the separate statutory provision governing remission.
